text:
marie: Quick sync - noisy short spikes caused two canaries to fully abort this morning. Both were <5min blips but our auto-rollback cut traffic. Thinking we need a risk-budget layer so brief noise doesn't trigger full evictions.
ajay: risk-budget? like tokens of forgiveness?
marie: exactly. Calling them 'grace_tokens' in the RFC. Each canary gets a pool; signals subtract tokens, healthy minutes add a small refill. Only when pool hits zero do we take hard actions.
linda: separate idea: treat latency and accuracy signals differently - latency blips might be transient, accuracy regressions need stricter handling.
marie: agreed. Configurable per-route signal sets and per-signal weights.
oliver: how to weight by traffic? If canary has 0.1% of traffic, one bad request could wipe it if we don't scale by volume.
marie: we weight penalties by request impact: weight = min(1.0, tokens / expected_tokens) * (1 + importance_multiplier). So big requests or high-importance routes consume more.
tim: what signals do we include initially? errors, eval regressions, latency percentiles?
marie: MVP signals: 1) error_rate (rolling 1m), 2) eval_regression_score (hourly), 3) p95_latency (1m). Each has threshold and penalty.
qa: what about recovery? If tokens slowly leak, how does the pool refill?
marie: refill_rate per healthy second and a passive decay on penalties (penalty halves every N minutes) so a past spike doesn't haunt forever. Max pool caps recovery too.
ajay: show a sample YAML config to be concrete.
marie: ```yaml
canary_grace:
  initial_tokens: 600
  max_tokens: 3600
  refill_per_second: 1
  signals:
    - id: error_rate
      window_secs: 60
      threshold: 0.01
      penalty: 50
    - id: eval_regression
      window_secs: 3600
      threshold: 0.03
      penalty: 300
    - id: p95_latency_ms
      window_secs: 60
      threshold: 800
      penalty: 20
  request_weighting: tokens
  exhaustion_sequence: [throttle_10pct, divert_shadow, rollback]
  tenant_fail_mode: fail_open
```
oliver: exhaustion_sequence is nice - soft mitigations first. Can we make it pluggable per tenant?
marie: yes tenant_fail_mode and per-tenant exhaustion_sequence override. Default public tenants fail_open; enterprise can set fail_closed.
tim: implementation: where state lives? local agent vs central ledger? We need fast decisions at the edge.
marie: hybrid model: local shim maintains a replica of the token pool for fast decisions and reconciles with central controller every 30s. Central is authoritative and can revoke immediately.
ajay: reconciliation semantics need to be clear: central overrides local. Also need monotonicity to prevent flipflopping.
marie: reconciliation behavior: central publishes authoritative token balance and last_update_ts. Local applies only if central timestamp is older than local's last action and otherwise adopts central. Central can push 'evict now' flag.
ora: network partition: local must have a configurable policy: operate on last-known tokens (fail-open) or lock down (fail-closed). Tenants choose. Document in ops playbook.
qa: tests: chaos scenarios to exercise brief spikes, long drifts, partitioned central, multi-variant shared pools.
marie: telemetry: emit canary_grace_tokens gauge, token_penalty_event counter (with signal tag), reconciliation_event, exhaustion_count, exhaustion_action_taken. UI shows sparkline with annotations.
ajay: proto changes? show a short sketch.
marie: ```proto
message GraceSignal {
  string id = 1;
  int32 window_secs = 2;
  double threshold = 3;
  int32 penalty = 4;
}
message CanaryGraceConfig {
  int32 initial_tokens = 1;
  int32 max_tokens = 2;
  int32 refill_per_second = 3;
  repeated GraceSignal signals = 4;
  repeated string exhaustion_sequence = 5;
}
```
marie: operationally, when exhaustion triggers rollback, controller should attach a breakdown: which signals used how many tokens and timestamps. That helps debugging.
oliver: question: shared vs per-variant pools when running A/B. Want default per-variant but ability to opt-in to a shared pool for related variants.
marie: default per-variant, with shared_pool_id optional. Shared pool decrements aggregate.
tim: cost/scale: more metrics and reconciliation traffic but we can sample or increase reconciliation interval for low-volume canaries.
linda: UX: change rollout page to show current tokens and a 'why' panel showing recent penalties. Good for operators.
ora: alerting: page on exhaustion only if action included rollback or tenant policy is fail_closed. Otherwise send non-paging warning.
ajay: important: add a 'grace buffer' for cold-starts so brand-new canaries don't immediately consume tokens during initial variability.
marie: adding "cold_start_protection": minutes of immunity that scales down over time.
qa: I'll add unit+integration tests in the canary harness and a chaos job that emits a 3-minute spike to ensure we don't rollback prematurely. Also partition test.
marie: next step: I'll write RFC covering config, state machine, reconciliation, telemetry, UI updates, and tests. Aim for draft by EOD Thursday. Any blockers?
linda: none here.:+1: 
ajay: go ahead. small naming nit: RFC can use 'grace_tokens' and yaml keep 'canary_grace' to avoid confusing existing 'canary_credit' fields.
marie: noted. I'll include migration notes for existing configs. Thanks all. End.
